title: Chociaż · mimo że
title_en: Although — the obstacle that did not stop it
note: C1-SPINE Block 9 unit 1; B2-SPINE inbox item 23, first half. TWO NEW WORDS AND ZERO NEW MORPHOLOGY - b2_conjunctions' idiom exactly: invariable joiners bolted onto clauses the learner can already build, with one contrast taught by table rather than derived. Neither word ever changes shape and neither changes anything in either clause. SCOPE HELD TO THE SPINE'S LETTER, AND THE FORK IS LOGGED: only chociaz and mimo ze are taught. choc (the everyday short form of chociaz) reports NEW and was deliberately NOT shown - showing it would put an untagged Polish string on screen, and teaching it would be a third word in a unit whose whole point is that it costs nothing. If James wants it, it is a one-line addition to slide 1 plus a teaches_lemmas entry. jednak, natomiast and pomimo are all NEW and out of scope by the same reasoning. MIMO ON ITS OWN IS FENCED. Bare mimo is a PREPOSITION governing the Genitive (mimo deszczu) - a new case governor, which would need its own row in data/case-map.json and is a second fact about the word. The unit teaches mimo ze as a single indivisible joiner and says on slide 2 that the two words are never separated. NO case-map row was added for this unit, which is correct: a conjunction governs nothing. THE ze INSIDE mimo ze IS NAMED, not left to collide. ze_clauses [147] taught ze as the complementiser after a verb of saying or knowing (Wiem, ze mama jest w domu); inside mimo ze it has no such job and there is no verb of saying anywhere near it. Slide 2 says this in one line - the chunk-versus-slot treatment dziekuje, ktorej and nowego all got. INTERCHANGEABILITY IS STATED, AND IT SHAPES THE QUIZ. chociaz and mimo ze are genuine everyday synonyms, so NO quiz item ever offers both as choices - marking one wrong where the other is right would be exactly the false-wrong James smoke-flagged on 2026-08-07. Every Kontrola item discriminates concession against an ALREADY-OWNED joiner (ale, a, bo, wiec, albo, i), which is also the sharper lesson: bo and chociaz take the same two clauses and claim opposite things about them. PISANIE FALLBACK, LOGGED PER THE REPAIR-QUEUE RULE: the unit has exactly two teaching-point strings, so only items 1 and 2 can carry them without breaking the no-duplicate-answers rule (norm() lowercases, so a sentence-initial Chociaz collides with the bare chociaz). The remaining ten clozes therefore blank the load-bearing form of the concessive clause with the joiner left VISIBLE in the frame, which is b1_vocative_chunks' precedent one level up. Sentence-level production of the joiners lives in Uzycie, where the whole sentence is typed. HOMOGRAPH WATCH: drogi is used in its TAUGHT sense, expensive (leaf_shopping_a1 [20]), never as anything to do with a road - C1-SPINE O13 names this as the trap, and the FEMININE droga was refused outright in a use item because the learner reads that string as the noun. CAUGHT IN SELF-REVIEW: a use item read 'tata czyta gazete' - gazete is NEW (only the plural gazety is taught), the same catch the which-case batch made at A2; replaced with ksiazke. gotowal (3sg masculine past of gotowac) is NOT in the pool either, so the past-tense use item runs on ugotowal (b2_aspect_prefixes [168]).

intro.title: Chociaż — the obstacle that did not stop it
intro.body:
You already join two clauses with ale. It sets two facts side by side and says the second goes against the first: Mam kawę, ale nie mam herbaty.

Concession is sharper than that. It marks one fact as the thing that should have stopped the other — and then says it did not.

chociaż — although, even though.

It is invariable. Nothing about it agrees with anything, and nothing in either clause changes shape because of it. Both halves are sentences you can already build on your own.

The clause it opens may stand first or second, and Polish writes the comma at the join either way.

rows: concession first
Chociaż byłem zmęczony, pracowałem.
Although I was tired, I worked.
concession second
Pracowałem, chociaż byłem zmęczony.
I worked, although I was tired.

examples.pl: Pomagam mamie, chociaż nie mam czasu.

intro.title: Mimo że — the same job, in two words
intro.title_pl: Mimo że pada deszcz, idę do parku.
intro.body:
mimo że does what chociaż does. In everyday Polish the two are interchangeable, and the choice between them is one of weight rather than of meaning: mimo że lands a little heavier, and it is the one you will more often meet in writing.

It is two words and they are never separated. The comma goes in front of the whole thing — never between mimo and że.

And notice what że is not doing here. On its own it attaches a clause to a verb of saying or knowing: Wiem, że mama jest w domu. Inside mimo że it has no such job, and there is no verb of saying anywhere near it. The two words together are the joiner.
intro.body_pl: Mimo że pada deszcz, idę do parku.

intro.title: Which joiner, and what each one claims
intro.body:
Four joiners, four different claims about how the two halves stand to each other. Only one line of this table is new today.

The pair worth the most attention is bo against chociaż. They take the same two clauses and say opposite things about them.

Idę do domu, bo jestem zmęczony — being tired is the reason I am going.

Pomagam mamie, chociaż nie mam czasu — not having time is the reason I should not be helping.
intro.body_pl: Ale · bo · więc · chociaż · mimo że

quiz.explain: Being tired is what should have stopped the working. Ale, więc and albo cannot open a sentence this way at all.
więc would make the illness the reason he is working. i would just add it on. Only the concessive says the illness argues against the working.

quiz.prompt: Mama pracuje, ___ tata gotuje. (and — two different things, no contradiction)
quiz.explain: Nothing here contradicts anything: two people, two jobs, side by side. chociaż would claim that Dad cooking should have stopped Mum working.

quiz.prompt: ___ jest zimno, dzieci są w parku. (even though)
quiz.explain: The cold is the obstacle. None of the other three can stand at the front of a sentence in this job.
Going home is the result of being tired, not something the tiredness argued against. Concession would turn the sentence upside down.
Cold coffee is a reason not to drink it. Saying it anyway is what a concessive is for.

quiz.prompt: ___ sklep jest zamknięty, kawiarnia jest otwarta. (although)
quiz.explain: One place shut, another open — the shut shop sets you up to expect the café shut too, and the concessive cancels that expectation.
This is the sharpest pair in the unit. bo makes the tiredness the reason for going; chociaż would make it the reason not to go, and the sentence would mean the opposite.
bo would say I am helping because I have no time, which is nonsense. Having no time is exactly what should have stopped me.
Two things joined inside one clause, not two clauses joined. A concessive needs a whole sentence on each side of it.
The lateness is the obstacle she worked through. Bo cannot open a sentence in this job.
The price is the reason not to buy it. Bo would make the price the reason to buy it.
